item.title: Yakan Tenun
item.description: Proudly displaying her “Os inalaman,” a tenun (Yakan weave) used as hip wraparound to complete a woman traditional attire, Mary Ann Taala, 45, is selling her produce at the provincial capitol of Basilan in Isabela City in time for the 18-Day Campaign to End Violence Against Women. The campaign runs from November 25 to December 12, 2025. MindaNews photo by JULES L. BENITEZ

item.title: Japan grants ₱325M for birth registration in Bangsamoro region
item.description: DAVAO CITY (MindaNews / 11 December) — The Japanese government has extended 858 million yen (₱325 million) to support birth registration and the campaign against statelessness in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). Japanese Minister for Economic Affairs Yokota Naobumi said the grant is part of Tokyo’s continuing support for the Bangsamoro peace […]

item.title: Diving for a Coin
item.description: Through the years, children from the sea community of Bajau have become a constant presence at the Isabela City wharf in Basilan, like the boys in this picture taken Thursday morning (11 December 2025), diving for coins thrown by travelers from arriving or departing passenger boats. MindaNews photo by JULES L. BENITEZ

item.title: Zambo steps up campaign vs. online child sexual exploitation
item.description: ZAMBOANGA CITY (MindaNews / 11 December) — The local government has intensified its campaign against online child sexual exploitation by equipping frontline responders with specialized training aimed at strengthening early detection, rapid intervention, and coordinated protection for vulnerable children. item.title: Human Rights Day Rally
item.description: Militant groups in Davao City call for justice, human rights and a just and lasting peace during a rally on International Human Rights Day on Wednesday (10 December 2025). MindaNews photo by CAROLYN O. ARGUILLAS

item.title: Philippine eagles retain rare genetics, offering boost to conservation efforts
item.description: GENERAL SANTOS CITY (MindaNews / 11 December) — Captive Philippine eagles (Pithecophaga jefferyi) preserve all known maternal genetic lineages of the critically endangered national bird, a new study by the University of the Philippines Mindanao, the Philippine Genome Center (PGC), and the Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) shows.
